heading: INT. SALON OF A GRAND HOUSE - NIGHT (1912)

units.text: INT. SALON OF A GRAND HOUSE - NIGHT (1912)
A gilded drawing room.
Fire in a marble hearth.
A piano shrouded in cloth.
Tall windows reveal fog on a dark street.
LADY ROSAMUND ASHFORD (40s, silk gown, pearls) stands at a writing desk, one hand pressed flat on an unsealed letter.
She does not sit.
A bell rings in the hall below.
She flinches, then composes herself.
"My dearest. By the time you read this, I will have crossed the water."
units.name: ROSAMUND

units.text: She closes her eyes.
Takes the letter, folds it, tucks it into the bodice of her gown.
Footsteps on the stair, slow, measured.
She straightens, smooths her skirts, turns toward the door with a hostess's smile.
Courage.
units.name: ROSAMUND

units.text: The footsteps pass the door and continue down the corridor.
The smile fades.
She laughs once, shakily.
She crosses to the fire.
Removes the letter and holds it over the flames.
At the last moment, she pulls it back.
"Do not look for me. I have taken the little blue case."
units.name: ROSAMUND

units.text: She goes back to the desk.
Sits.
Unfolds the letter, smooths it, and reads it again from the top.
Her lips move.
The fire shifts.
Outside in the hall, the bell rings once more.
She does not rise.
